fields.why: • Under the existing control philosophy, 222-SC-002 and 222-SC-502 continue running following a 222-CV-006 process stoppage. A trial 222-CV-006 Running process interlock with a two (2) second off-delay is proposed to assess whether it reduces material accumulation within the CV-006 feed chutes.
fields.design:
• Add a two (2) second process shutdown delay to 222-SC-002 HPGR Screen 1 and 222-SC-502 HPGR Screen 2 following loss of the 222-CV-006 HPGR Feed Conveyor Running status.

SCADA Reference Pages:
• 222-CV-006 HPGR Feed Conveyor: [Image in form – see source document]
• 222-SC-002 HPGR Screen 1:
 o There are currently no start permissives or process interlocks.
• 222-SC-502 HPGR Screen 2:
 o There are currently no start permissives or process interlocks.

SCADA Changes:
• 222-SC-002 HPGR Screen 1 – Add one Process Interlock to the faceplate:
 o 222-CV-006: HPGR Feed Conveyor Running (With 2 second delay)
• 222-SC-502 HPGR Screen 2 – Add one Process Interlock to the faceplate:
 o 222-CV-006: HPGR Feed Conveyor Running (With 2 second delay)
fields.impact: HPGR screens 1 and 2 will stop about 2 seconds after CV-006 stops instead of continuing to run.
fields.testCriteria:
- Normal operation: screen starts, runs and stops normally from PCS/SCADA
- Process shutdown delay: screen stops ~2 s after 222-CV-006 stops
- Safety shutdown: screen stops immediately with no delay on E-Stop or pull-wire
- Alarm and status verification: no unexpected alarms
- Record Pass/Fail for 222-SC-002 and 222-SC-502 at each step
fields.scheduleNote: Waiting for a test period to be arranged by Mech Projects.
